cards.explanation: The answer is a voice of triumph, friends! Verse 1 says, "Clap your hands, all you peoples; shout unto God with a voice of triumph." That's not a polite little cough into your fist. That's the kind of shout that rattles the cooling racks, and I bet my mustache would be clapping right along.

The answer is all the earth, friends! Verse 2 says, "How awesome is the LORD Most High, the great King over all the earth!" Not one corner left out. Not even the corner of the earth where somebody still hasn't found their keys.

The answer is True! Verse 3 says, "He subdues nations beneath us, and peoples under our feet." The psalm is singing about what God does for His people. You can't beat that for a verse that starts with a victory.
The answer is False, friends! Verse 4 says, "He chooses our inheritance for us…" God does the choosing, not the people. Nobody is standing there with a clipboard picking their own.
The answer is that He loves him! Verse 4 says, "He chooses our inheritance for us, the pride of Jacob, whom He loves." Love is the word the psalm uses. It sits right there in the verse.

The answer is shouts of joy, friends! Verse 5 says, "God has ascended amid shouts of joy, the LORD with the sound of the horn." Joy all around, and a horn blowing too. That's a sound I'd want to hear.

The answer is True! Verse 8 says, "God reigns over the nations; God is seated on His holy throne." The psalm gives us a picture of a King who is seated and reigning. That's the picture, friends, right there in the verse.

The answer is the God of Abraham! Verse 9 says the nobles "…have assembled as the people of the God of Abraham…" Abraham, the one Genesis 12 starts calling out of his homeland. The psalm ties this whole gathering back to that old family name.

The answer is God, friends! Verse 9 says, "for the shields of the earth belong to God; He is highly exalted." The whole psalm has been saying He is King of all the earth, so this fits right in. Even the shields are His.
